analysis.title: UBS House View - Daily US: Higher oil and AI concerns drive risk-off move
key_insights: Tech shares fell Thursday on concerns over financing and returns from the next phase of the AI buildout. The Nasdaq fell 2.6%, its steepest one-day decline since 5 June, and the Philadelphia Semiconductor Index dropped 6.7% to its lowest level since July.
Meta shares fell 7% after results, reversing an initially positive after-market reaction as concerns grew over the company's rising capital expenditure plan.
The weakness was concentrated in technology. Two-thirds of S&P 500 constituents advanced and the equal-weighted index gained 0.8%.

Brent crude rose 4% to a five-month high of USD 113/bbl on renewed energy supply concerns. The risk-off move pushed the 10-year US Treasury yield down nearly 17 bp to 4.95%, the largest daily decline since August 2024.

UBS view is unchanged: robust earnings should continue to support equities, AI demand remains strong, bond yields provide attractive income, and geopolitics alone does not justify a broadly defensive stance.

UBS expects Q3 S&P 500 EPS to grow 28% y/y, driven by AI demand, an improving industrial cycle and resilient higher-income consumers. Semiconductors are expected to contribute about half of that growth. Average cloud revenue growth is forecast to accelerate from 48% in the June quarter to 58% y/y in the September quarter.

Risks are rising among neoclouds (single-product firms renting compute capacity), where funding pressure and execution risk could reinforce each other. UBS limits neocloud exposure and favors well-funded hyperscalers.
Cyclical support: nine consecutive months of expansion in the ISM Manufacturing new-orders component and 6% y/y growth in September US retail sales support robust cyclical earnings.

The 10-year Treasury yield reached 5.36% in early October, its highest since 2002, before falling to 4.95%. UBS rates fixed income Attractive. Capital losses would offset one year of income only if 2-, 5- and 10-year yields rose about 246, 109 and 63 bp. UBS expects a moderate decline in yields over 12 months and favors medium and longer-duration high-quality bonds, but is cautious on the longest maturities given fiscal concerns and issuance.

Middle East crude and refined product exports recovered to about 80% of pre-conflict levels in September on partial restoration of Hormuz flows and pipeline rerouting. In October, increased Iranian attacks on shipping in Hormuz and the failure of Russia and Ukraine to agree an energy-infrastructure ceasefire pushed prices up again.

Oil is up about USD 40/bbl on average vs last year. UBS estimates this alone could cut global GDP growth by 0.3-0.5 percentage points, but consumption has stayed resilient. Barring a significant and sustained rise, the headwind should fade over 12 months.

Positioning: diversified cyclical and structural growth exposure while reducing concentrated single-stock positions. Favors well-funded hyperscalers, high-quality semiconductor and hardware beneficiaries and defensive tech over neoclouds. Broad commodity exposure is suggested for diversification and protection against a prolonged energy-supply disruption.

The 10-year French-German spread briefly widened to 178 bp, a 15-year high. The French 10-year yield hit 5.14% (highest since 2002) before easing to 5.06%, and the 2-year rose to 3.88% before falling to 3.77%. The CAC 40 fell 1.4% Thursday and was down a further 0.5% Friday.

UBS base case is that French stress does not become a broader European funding crisis, citing well-capitalized banks, limited domestic sovereign exposure, European safeguards and solid demand at France's latest debt sale. It cannot rule out higher yields and expects European borrowing costs to fall into next year.

Safe-haven currencies rallied except the US dollar. USDJPY fell 0.9% to 156.76, its biggest daily drop in about a month, and USD fell 0.5% vs CHF to 0.82. UBS sees near-term USD yield support, especially vs CHF, but expects USDCHF to decline over time.
UBS forecasts USDCHF at 0.81 end-December and 0.79 end-March 2027, and USDJPY at 160 end-December and 158 thereafter. It would not chase the yen rally.

Chinese stocks rebounded Friday after entering a technical bear market Thursday. The CSI 300 rose 1.7% Friday after a decline of more than 20% since June. Causes cited: possible extension of export VAT rebate cuts, internet regulation sensitivity, speculation on selling tied to the offshore tax declaration deadline, and reduced stimulus expectations after better-than-expected Q3 GDP.

UBS sees the China correction as policy concern, positioning and risk reduction rather than broad fundamental deterioration. It favors A-shares over H-shares and sees improved A-share entry points in semiconductor equipment, hardware, advanced manufacturing, innovative pharma, contract manufacturers and large Chinese banks.

sector_views.rationale: Favors well-funded hyperscalers, high-quality semiconductor and hardware beneficiaries and defensive tech. Semiconductors are expected to contribute about half of Q3 S&P 500 EPS growth.
Capital-intensive single-product compute renters face funding pressure and execution risk. UBS limits exposure.
Nine months of ISM new-orders expansion and 6% y/y September retail sales growth support robust earnings.
Rated Attractive. Yields give an income cushion, and UBS favors medium and longer-duration high-quality bonds but is cautious on the longest maturities.
Broad commodity exposure can diversify portfolios and protect against a prolonged energy-supply disruption.
Selective approach favoring A-shares over H-shares, with semiconductor equipment, hardware, advanced manufacturing, innovative pharma, contract manufacturers and large banks.

earnings_insights: Meta shares fell 7% after its results as concerns grew over its rising capital expenditure plan, reversing an initially positive after-market reaction.
UBS forecast: Q3 S&P 500 EPS +28% y/y (estimate), with semiconductors contributing about half of the growth.

macro_indicators.interpretation: Fell nearly 17 bp on Thursday, the largest daily decline since August 2024, in a flight to safety. It was 5.36% in early October, the highest since 2002.
Up 4% to a five-month high on energy supply concerns. Oil is up about USD 40/bbl on average vs last year, which UBS estimates could cut global GDP growth by 0.3-0.5 pp in isolation.
Supports UBS view of robust cyclical earnings.
Reduced expectations for near-term stimulus, contributing to the equity pullback.
UBS estimate driven by AI demand, industrial cycle and higher-income consumers.
UBS expects the dollar to weaken vs the franc as Fed support fades and the SNB likely tightens.
BOJ normalization limits renewed yen weakness, but UBS would not chase the rally.

risk_factors: Funding pressures and execution risks among neoclouds.
Rising AI capital expenditure and uncertain returns on the next phase of the AI buildout.
Higher energy prices as a headwind to growth and inflation, with escalation in Hormuz and no Russia-Ukraine energy ceasefire.
French fiscal and political stress could keep European sovereign markets volatile, with a further rise in yields possible.
Fiscal concerns and elevated issuance weigh on the longest-maturity bonds.
China export VAT rebate changes, internet regulation and offshore tax declaration-related selling.
vol_and_positioning: UBS says higher FX volatility may give investors opportunities to use structured strategies to harvest yield, subject to the risks of options.
UBS recommends reducing concentrated single-stock positions.
geopolitical: Increased Iranian attacks on shipping in the Strait of Hormuz in October.
Russia and Ukraine failed to agree a ceasefire on energy infrastructure.
Middle East crude and refined product exports recovered to about 80% of pre-conflict levels in September via partial Hormuz restoration and pipeline rerouting.
French political gridlock, fiscal pressure and prospect of further protests ahead of next year's presidential election.
China export VAT rebate cuts that could extend to other industries, and renewed sensitivity to internet regulation.

tension_points.bull_case: AI demand remains strong, Q3 S&P 500 EPS is forecast to grow 28% y/y with cloud revenue growth accelerating to 58% y/y, and well-funded hyperscalers and semiconductors are favored.
tension_points.bear_case: Investors question the financing and returns of the next phase of AI capex (Meta fell 7% on rising capex plans) and neoclouds face funding and execution risks.

tension_points.bull_case: Well-capitalized banks, limited domestic sovereign exposure, European safeguards and solid demand at France's latest debt sale make gradual pressure more likely than a funding crisis.
tension_points.bear_case: Political gridlock, fiscal pressure and protests ahead of next year's presidential election could push yields higher and keep markets volatile.

theme_stances.key_argument: Earnings remain robust and AI demand strong, but selectivity is needed, favoring well-funded hyperscalers over capital-intensive neoclouds.
theme_stances.evidence: greater selectivity is needed within the AI ecosystem

theme_stances.key_argument: Repriced yields restore return potential, and a capital loss large enough to offset a year of income is unlikely.
theme_stances.evidence: We continue to rate fixed income as Attractive

theme_stances.key_argument: The current pressure is unlikely to become a broader European funding crisis.
